senses.gloss: m. (ספג, cmp. ספח) a porous luxuriant growth, mushroom; sponge, any sponge-like material; wiper.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2:23">Y. Sabb. VII, 10ᵃ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>ההן דגזז ס׳ וכ׳</he> he who cuts mushrooms etc. (on the Sabbath) is guilty of the acts of harvesting and of planting (the cutting being the means of advancing the growth).

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 115b">B. Kam. 115ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Sukkah 50a">Succ. 50ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 587:5">Yalk. Mal. 587</cite> <he>ארס … דומה לס׳ וכ׳</he> the venom of the serpent (on top of liquids) resembles a fungus (Ar.: a veil-like growth on the head of a certain sea-fish) and remains floating &c.; (Y. Ter. VII, 45ᵈ bot. <he>עומד כסבכה</he>, v. <cite ref="O00068"><he>סְבָכָה</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 9:4">Kel. IX, 4</cite> <he>ס׳ שבלע וכ׳</he> a mushroom which has absorbed unclean liquids, though it is dry on the outside etc.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 21:3">Sabb. XXI, 3</cite> <he>ס׳ אם יש לו עור וכ׳</he> a sponge (used for sucking up liquids), if it has leather handles etc.

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 5:3">Tosef. ib. V</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 6:3">VI</cite>), 3 <he>ס׳ שע״ג המכה</he> an absorbent substance (wool) put on a wound. Y. ib. XVII, 15ᶜ top <he>ונתן עליה ס׳ יבש</he> and he put on it a dry sucker (compress); <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 15:4">Lev. R. s. 15</cite>; <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 4:23">Lam. R. to IV, 20</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:15">Ab. V, 15</cite> <he>ס׳ שהוא סופג וכ׳</he> (a scholar indiscriminately cramming his mind is called) a sponge, because he absorbs every thing.—Pl. <he>סְפוֹגִים</he>, <he>סְפוֹגִין</he>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 16:4:4">Y. Yeb. XVI, 15ᵈ</cite> top <he>רצו לחתוך ס׳</he> (divers) wanted to cut sponges.
<cite ref="Shabbat 129b:13">Sabb. 129ᵇ</cite> <he>ס׳ של צמר</he> tufts of wool; (Tosef. ib. XV (XVI), 3 <cite ref="K00911"><he>כסות</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 18a:12">Ab. Zar. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>הביאו ס׳ של צמד וכ׳</he> they took tufts of wool, soaked them with water, and put them onhis heart; a. e.—[Σπόγγος, σφόγγος seems to be of Semitic origin.]
